claim: Neumann's genus-three table has three realizable polynomial ambient types, of intrinsic degrees four, six (cable), and seven (hyperelliptic); only the last is assumed in the scoped sextic-conductor theorem.
inspection: Internal rendered-page inspection and algebraic source-form transcription.

sources.title: Complex algebraic plane curves via their links at infinity
sources.author: Walter D. Neumann

inspected.content: Table lists the three realizable genus-three rows: torus (4,3), cable (3,2;2,3), and torus (7,2), of intrinsic degrees four, six, and seven. The (3,2;3,1) row is not realizable. The paragraph before the table states ambient polynomial-equivalence scope.
The first displayed polynomial is the degree-six cable form f1, including d!=0; the coefficient-computation explanation follows.
Corrected Lemma7.1: a reduced fibre with a knot at infinity has a good defining polynomial.

applicability: The generic exact conductor degree six gives normalization defect three on the source line.
Normalization is the affine line with one place at infinity; the actual Keller restriction is immersed.
The generic ambient hyperelliptic degree-seven type is an explicit additional hypothesis, not a conclusion for all defect-three orders.
Its affine-line normalization has canonical form X=u^2+gamma,Y=u*f(u^2),deg f=3,f(0)!=0.
Other genus-three ambient types are invoked only to prevent a special fixed central three-node order from switching to intrinsic degree below seven.
not_assumed: All genus-three or all three-nodal embeddings are not declared ambient equivalent.
No uniform polynomial target automorphism over the source parameter is assumed.
The conditional parametric-lines classification is not used.
